questions.topic: Case Study – Dynamic E-Commerce Ltd. (Ultra Vires, Registered Office Shift, Interim Dividend)
questions.case_context: Dynamic E-Commerce Ltd. incorporated 1st April 2020. MOA capital clause: ₹1,00,00,000 (undivided). AOA capital clause: ₹1,00,00,000 divided into 8,00,000 equity shares of ₹10 each and 20,000 preference shares of ₹10 each. Financial institution refused to subscribe to preference shares claiming MOA is ambiguous. Company wants to shift registered office from Pune to Mumbai (both in Maharashtra). Board intends to declare interim dividend for FY 2022-23.

sub_questions.question_text: Whether the contention of the financial institution in refusing to subscribe to the issue of preference shares of the company is valid?

key_points: Ultra vires doctrine explanation: Acts contrary to Companies Act, MOA, or AOA are ultra vires and void
Ultra vires the MOA: Act not stated in MOA as objects or powers is prohibited; void and cannot be ratified
Ultra vires the AOA: If acts are outside AOA but within MOA, they are ultra vires AOA but can be ratified by special resolution
Key case: Re. South Durham Brewery Company [(1875) LR 7 HL 65c]: MOA was unclear about classes of shares; AOA gave power to issue different classes of shares
Court held: Articles can be used to EXPLAIN AMBIGUITY contained in the Memorandum. The two documents must be read TOGETHER at least to explain ambiguity in MOA
In this case: MOA is unclear about class of shares (ambiguous) but AOA clearly states equity and preference shares
Conclusion: AOA can be used to explain the ambiguity in MOA. Offering preference shares is NOT ultra vires. Contention of financial institution is NOT VALID
legal_provisions: Re. South Durham Brewery Company (1875) LR 7 HL 65c
Memorandum and Articles of Association interpretation
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: The financial institution's contention is NOT valid. Under the South Durham Brewery case, when MOA is ambiguous, Articles of Association can be used to explain/supplement the MOA. Here, though MOA does not specify the class of shares, the AOA clearly provides for both equity and preference shares. Reading both documents together, offering preference shares is NOT ultra vires.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: Explains ultra vires doctrine + cites South Durham case + correctly concludes contention is invalid
evaluation_criteria.good: Correct conclusion with South Durham principle even without case name
evaluation_criteria.partial: Knows articles can supplement MOA but does not apply correctly

sub_questions.question_text: Compliance requirement for shifting registered office from Pune to Mumbai (both in Maharashtra, different ROC jurisdictions).

key_points: Change is within same State (Maharashtra) but from jurisdiction of ROC Pune to ROC Mumbai
Section 12(5) Companies Act 2013 + Rule 28 Companies (Incorporation) Rules 2014: Change from jurisdiction of one Registrar to another within same State requires CONFIRMATION OF THE REGIONAL DIRECTOR
Application to be made to Regional Director in Form INC-23 with fee

Documents to be attached with application: (a) Board Resolution for shifting; (b) Special Resolution of members approving shifting; (c) Declaration by KMP or two directors that company has not defaulted on dues to workmen and has consent of creditors or made provision for payment; (d) Declaration not to seek change in jurisdiction of Court where prosecution cases are pending; (e) Acknowledged copy of intimation to Chief Secretary of State about proposed shifting and that employees' interest is not adversely affected
Regional Director shall pass order (approving or rejecting) within 15 DAYS of receipt of application
Certified copy of order to be filed in Form INC-28 with Registrar of State within 30 DAYS from receipt of certified copy of order
Section 12(6): Confirmation communicated within 30 days; company files with Registrar within 60 days of confirmation; Registrar certifies within 30 days
LEGAL OFFICER'S ADVICE IS INCORRECT: Cannot shift by passing only a board resolution
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: Shifting from Pune to Mumbai (different ROC jurisdictions within Maharashtra) requires: Board Resolution + Special Resolution of members + Application to Regional Director (Form INC-23) + specified attachments. RD passes order within 15 days. Company files Form INC-28 with Registrar within 30 days of receiving order. Legal Officer's advice (only board resolution needed) is INCORRECT.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: Identifies RD approval required + Form INC-23 + special resolution + all attachments + timelines + INC-28 filing
evaluation_criteria.good: RD approval + special resolution + Form INC-23 with 3-4 attachments
evaluation_criteria.partial: Knows RD approval needed but misses form numbers or attachments
evaluation_criteria.minimal: Knows it's more than just a board resolution

sub_questions.question_text: Explain 'Divisible Profit'. Can interim dividend be paid out of free reserves in event of loss or inadequacy of profit?

key_points: Divisible Profits: Profits which the law allows the company to distribute to shareholders by way of dividend. Palmer's Company Law: 'divisible profits' and 'profits in the legal sense' are synonymous
Divisible profits = net proceeds after deducting necessary outgoings without which proceeds could not be earned (Bharat Insurance Co. Ltd. v. CIT 1931)
Divisible profits = that portion of profit distributable legally among shareholders (after provisions for past losses and reserves)
Interim Dividend – Section 123(3) Companies Act 2013: Board may declare interim dividend during any financial year OR at any time during period from closure of financial year till holding of AGM

Sources for interim dividend: (a) Surplus in P&L Account; (b) Profits of the financial year for which interim dividend is sought; (c) Profits generated in FY till the quarter preceding date of declaration

If company has incurred LOSS during current FY up to end of quarter preceding date of declaration: Interim dividend shall NOT be declared at rate HIGHER than AVERAGE DIVIDENDS declared during immediately preceding 3 FYs
SS-3 provides: In event of LOSS or INADEQUACY OF PROFITS during a financial year, NO INTERIM DIVIDEND shall be declared/paid OUT OF FREE RESERVES
Conclusion: NO – interim dividend CANNOT be declared out of free reserves in event of loss or inadequacy of profit
legal_provisions: Bharat Insurance Co. Ltd. v. CIT (1931)
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: Divisible profits are legally distributable profits after deducting necessary outgoings and making provisions for losses/reserves. Under S.123(3) CA 2013, interim dividend can be declared from P&L surplus or current year profits. However, SS-3 clearly states that NO interim dividend shall be declared/paid out of FREE RESERVES in event of loss or inadequacy of profits. Hence, the board CANNOT declare interim dividend from free reserves in such event.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: Defines divisible profit correctly + S.123(3) sources + SS-3 prohibition on free reserves in loss + correct conclusion
evaluation_criteria.good: Correct definition + S.123(3) + SS-3 prohibition
evaluation_criteria.partial: Correct conclusion on free reserves but incomplete definition
evaluation_criteria.minimal: Only defines dividend or only mentions S.123

questions.topic: Investigation, Secretarial Audit, Charge Satisfaction, Financial Statement Authentication

sub_questions.question_text: Recognised trade union applied before Tribunal for investigation of Water Purifier Ltd. Company objects saying trade union has no locus standi. Examine admissibility.

key_points: Section 213, Companies Act 2013: Tribunal may order investigation into affairs of company

Such order can be made on application by 'ANY OTHER PERSON' (not restricted to members or creditors) if satisfied that circumstances suggest business is conducted with intent to defraud creditors, members or others, or for fraudulent/unlawful purpose, or in manner oppressive to members, or company formed for fraudulent purpose
Since trade union alleged business conducted for fraudulent/unlawful purpose AND defaulted on payment of dues to workmen
Conclusion: Company's objection is NOT TENABLE. Application of recognised trade union is ADMISSIBLE
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: Section 213 CA 2013 allows 'any other person' (not just members or creditors) to apply for investigation if circumstances suggest fraud/unlawful business. The recognised trade union qualifies. The company's objection on locus standi is not tenable and the application is admissible.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: Cites S.213 + 'any other person' language + correct conclusion
evaluation_criteria.good: Correct conclusion with general S.213 reference
evaluation_criteria.partial: Correct conclusion without legal basis

sub_questions.question_text: AB Pvt. Ltd. is unlisted material subsidiary of HD Ltd. (listed entity). CS believes secretarial audit for AB not required as it is private and unlisted. Is secretarial audit for AB voluntary? Explain material subsidiary. Also explain timeline for secretarial compliance report by listed entity.

key_points: Section 204(1) CA 2013 + Rule 9: Secretarial audit mandatory for: every listed company + public companies with paid-up capital ≥ ₹50 crore + public companies with turnover ≥ ₹250 crore + companies with outstanding loans/borrowings from banks/PFIs ≥ ₹100 crore
AB Pvt. Ltd. does NOT qualify under S.204 CA 2013 as it is private and unlisted

BUT: Regulation 24A, SEBI (LODR) Regulations 2015: Every listed entity AND its MATERIAL UNLISTED SUBSIDIARIES incorporated in India shall undertake secretarial audit and annex secretarial audit report with the annual report of listed entity
AB Pvt. Ltd. is a material unlisted subsidiary of HD Ltd. (listed entity) → Secretarial Audit is COMPULSORY, NOT VOLUNTARY
CS's view is INCORRECT
Secretarial Compliance Report: Every listed entity shall submit to stock exchanges within 60 DAYS from end of each financial year

Material Subsidiary definition: Regulation 24(1) SEBI LODR – subsidiary whose INCOME OR NET WORTH exceeds 20% of the consolidated income or net worth of the listed company and its subsidiaries in the immediately preceding accounting year
legal_provisions: Rule 9, Companies (Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel) Rules, 2014
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: CS's conviction is WRONG. Under Reg. 24A SEBI LODR, material unlisted subsidiaries of listed entities MUST undergo secretarial audit. AB Pvt. Ltd., as a material unlisted subsidiary of listed HD Ltd., must comply. Secretarial compliance report must be submitted to stock exchanges within 60 days of year-end. Material subsidiary: income or net worth > 20% of consolidated income/net worth of listed company and subsidiaries in preceding year.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: Reg. 24A SEBI LODR + compulsory conclusion + 60-day timeline + material subsidiary definition with 20% threshold
evaluation_criteria.good: Reg. 24A + compulsory + material subsidiary definition
evaluation_criteria.partial: Knows it's compulsory under SEBI but incomplete definition
evaluation_criteria.minimal: Only says CA 2013 doesn't require it without SEBI LODR angle

sub_questions.question_text: Edge Ltd. repaid ₹50 crore loan. Wants to file satisfaction of charge ONLY after receiving 'no due certificate' from bank. Will delay attract liability?

key_points: Section 82 CA 2013 + Rule 8 Companies (Registration of Charges) Rules 2014
Company or charge-holder shall give intimation to Registrar within 30 DAYS from date of payment/satisfaction in full in Form CHG-4
Registrar may allow intimation within 300 DAYS of satisfaction on payment of additional fees
On receipt, Registrar issues notice to charge-holder to show cause within 14 days why payment should not be recorded
However: Notice is NOT sent if Form CHG-4 is filed along with LETTER FROM CHARGE-HOLDER stating amount has been satisfied (mandatory attachment)
Key conclusion: Filing of satisfaction of charge does NOT depend on obtaining 'no due certificate' from bank
In absence of bank's letter, Registrar gets confirmation from bank directly
Edge Ltd. SHOULD HAVE filed within time limit; Registrar would obtain confirmation from bank
Edge Ltd. IS LIABLE for delayed filing and must pay ADDITIONAL FEES for delayed filing
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: Under S.82 CA 2013, satisfaction of charge must be filed within 30 days (extendable to 300 days with additional fees). Filing is NOT conditional on receiving a no-due certificate – the Registrar issues notice to charge-holder to confirm. Edge Ltd. cannot delay filing while waiting for the bank's certificate. The company IS LIABLE for delayed filing and must pay additional fees.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: S.82 + 30-day timeline + no dependency on bank certificate + liability for delay + additional fees
evaluation_criteria.good: S.82 + correct conclusion that delay attracts liability
evaluation_criteria.partial: Knows filing needed within time but misses no-dependency on bank certificate

sub_questions.question_text: Mithi Sugar Ltd.: 4 directors (A,B,C,D) + MD (Mr. R) + Company Secretary (Mr. Anupam). Financial statements authenticated only by directors A and B. Examine validity.

key_points: Section 134(1) CA 2013: Financial statements shall be approved by Board BEFORE signing

Signing on behalf of Board by: (a) Chairperson if authorised by Board; OR (b) TWO directors out of which ONE shall be MANAGING DIRECTOR (if any); AND (c) CEO, CFO, and Company Secretary wherever appointed
Section 134(6): Board's report signed by chairperson or at least TWO directors, ONE of whom shall be Managing Director
In this case: Mr. R (MD) must be ONE of the two directors signing financial statements. Mr. Anupam (Company Secretary) must also sign.
Authentication done only by Mr. A and Mr. B (neither is MD, CS not included) is NOT VALID
Mr. R (MD) and Mr. Anupam (CS) must both sign along with one other director
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: Under S.134(1), financial statements must be signed by two directors (one being MD) AND the CS and CFO wherever appointed. Authentication by only A and B (excluding MD and CS) is NOT VALID. Mr. R (MD) must be one signatory, and Mr. Anupam (CS) must also sign.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: S.134(1) + MD requirement + CS requirement + correct conclusion of invalidity
evaluation_criteria.good: S.134(1) + identifies missing MD and CS + correct conclusion
evaluation_criteria.partial: Knows authentication is invalid but incomplete reasoning

sub_questions.question_text: If company is OPC with only one Director who authenticated Financial Statement and Board's Report – validity?

key_points: Section 134(1) CA 2013: In case of ONE PERSON COMPANY, financial statements shall be signed by ONLY ONE DIRECTOR
For submission to auditor for report
In the given case: OPC has only one director who has authenticated FS and Board's Report
Conclusion: Authentication is IN ORDER and VALID
legal_provisions: Section 134(1), Companies Act, 2013 – proviso for OPC
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: For a One Person Company, Section 134(1) specifically provides that financial statements shall be signed by only ONE director. Hence, authentication by the single director is valid and in order.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: Cites S.134(1) OPC exception + correct conclusion of validity
evaluation_criteria.good: Correct conclusion with OPC reference
evaluation_criteria.partial: Says valid but without citing specific OPC provision

questions.topic: Books & Papers of Amalgamated Company, Dormant Company, Deposits

sub_questions.question_text: 10 years after Y Ltd. took over X Ltd., Board resolved to destroy books and papers of X Ltd. considering 8-year preservation rule. Validity?

key_points: Section 239 CA 2013 (Chapter XV – Compromises, Arrangements and Amalgamations)
Books and papers of a company amalgamated with or whose shares acquired by another company shall NOT BE DISPOSED OF without PRIOR PERMISSION of the CENTRAL GOVERNMENT

Before granting permission, Central Government may appoint a person to EXAMINE the books and papers to ascertain whether they contain evidence of commission of an offence in connection with promotion, formation, management of transferor company or its amalgamation/acquisition
Regular 8-year preservation rule for books of account does NOT apply to this scenario
Conclusion: Decision of Board of Y Ltd. is NOT VALID. Prior permission of Central Government is required before disposing of books of X Ltd.
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: Section 239 CA 2013 specifically overrides the general 8-year rule. Books and papers of the transferor company (X Ltd.) CANNOT be disposed of without PRIOR PERMISSION of the Central Government. The Board's decision is NOT valid. Y Ltd. must obtain Central Government permission before destroying X Ltd.'s records.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: Cites S.239 + prior permission of CG required + CG examination process + correct conclusion
evaluation_criteria.good: S.239 + CG permission required + correct conclusion
evaluation_criteria.partial: Knows it can't be destroyed without permission but unsure which authority
evaluation_criteria.minimal: Says Board's decision is wrong without legal basis

sub_questions.question_text: Explain the term 'Dormant Company'.

key_points: Section 455(1) CA 2013: Company formed for future project or to hold asset or intellectual property with NO SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING TRANSACTION can apply for dormant status

Explanation (i) to S.455: 'Inactive company' means company which has NOT been carrying on business or operation, OR has not made any significant accounting transaction during last 2 FYs, OR has not filed financial statements and annual returns during last 2 FYs
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: Dormant company under S.455 is a company formed for a future project or holding an asset/IP with no significant accounting transaction, or an inactive company that has not carried on business, made significant accounting transactions, or filed returns for the last 2 years.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: Cites S.455 + both elements (future project type + inactive company definition)
evaluation_criteria.good: S.455 + correct definition
evaluation_criteria.partial: Correct definition without section citation

sub_questions.question_text: Whether payment of applicable filing fees to ROC can be considered a 'significant accounting transaction'?

key_points: Explanation (ii) to Section 455 CA 2013: 'Significant accounting transaction' means any transaction OTHER THAN: (a) payment of fees by company to Registrar; (b) payments to fulfil requirements of this Act or any other law; (c) allotment of shares to fulfil requirements of this Act; (d) payments for maintenance of office and records
Conclusion: Payment of applicable filing fees to ROC CANNOT be considered as significant accounting transaction
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: Under Explanation (ii) to S.455, 'significant accounting transaction' EXCLUDES payment of fees by a company to the Registrar. Hence, filing fees paid to ROC is NOT a significant accounting transaction.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: Cites Explanation (ii) to S.455 + lists the 4 excluded categories + correct conclusion
evaluation_criteria.good: Correct conclusion with Explanation (ii) reference
evaluation_criteria.partial: Correct conclusion without specific provision

sub_questions.question_text: Sanjay Diagnostic Ltd. obtained 82% consent from shareholders through notice instead of passing a special resolution. Is application in order?

key_points: Rule 3, Companies (Miscellaneous) Rules 2014: Application for dormant company status can be made EITHER by: (a) passing a SPECIAL RESOLUTION in general meeting; OR (b) issuing notice to ALL SHAREHOLDERS and obtaining consent of at least 3/4th (75%) shareholders IN VALUE
Sanjay Diagnostic Ltd. issued notice to all shareholders and obtained 82% consent (value) = exceeds 3/4th requirement
Conclusion: Application is IN ORDER
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: Under Rule 3, a dormant company application can be made by special resolution OR by obtaining consent of at least 3/4th (75%) shareholders by value through notice. Sanjay Diagnostic obtained 82% consent (> 75%) through notice to all shareholders. The application is IN ORDER.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: Cites Rule 3 + both alternate methods + 3/4th threshold + 82% > 75% + correct conclusion
evaluation_criteria.good: Correct conclusion with 3/4th threshold and Rule 3 reference
evaluation_criteria.partial: Correct conclusion but incorrect threshold mentioned

sub_questions.question_text: XYZ Ltd. – which of 5 listed receipts are 'deposits' and which must be reported in DPT-3?
receipts_listed: 1. Amount received against issue of commercial paper
2. Amount received from a director who furnished written declaration that it is not from borrowed funds
3. Amount from employee not exceeding annual salary (non-interest-bearing security deposit under employment contract)
4. Term deposits from members for 2 years

key_points: Section 2(31) CA 2013 + Rule 2(1)(c) Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules 2014: 'Deposit' includes any receipt of money by way of deposit/loan or any other form but EXCLUDES certain receipts
Receipt 1 (Commercial paper): EXEMPT from deposit – NOT a deposit
Receipt 2 (Director with declaration): EXEMPT – NOT a deposit
Receipt 3 (Employee security deposit ≤ annual salary under employment contract): EXEMPT – NOT a deposit
Receipt 4 (Term deposits from members for 2 years): DEPOSIT
Receipt 5 (Public deposits for 36 months): DEPOSIT
DPT-3 reporting: Rule 16 Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules 2014 – Form DPT-3 shall be used for filing return of deposit OR particulars of transaction NOT considered as deposit OR both
Explanation: Form DPT-3 is to be used for ALL transactions (whether deposit or not)
Conclusion: ALL 5 receipts (Serial No. 1 to 5) must be reported in Form DPT-3
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: Receipts 1, 2, 3 are NOT deposits (exempt categories). Receipts 4 and 5 ARE deposits. However, Form DPT-3 must be filed for ALL transactions – whether or not they qualify as deposits – as the form covers both deposits and transactions not considered as deposits. ALL 5 receipts must be reported in DPT-3.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: Correctly classifies all 5 receipts (1,2,3 = not deposits; 4,5 = deposits) + all 5 in DPT-3
evaluation_criteria.good: Correctly classifies 4-5 receipts + DPT-3 for all
evaluation_criteria.partial: Correctly classifies 2-3 receipts but misses DPT-3 scope
evaluation_criteria.minimal: Only identifies deposits without exempt categories

questions.topic: Employee Protection (S.218), Alteration of Object Clause (S.13), Minor as Member – OR – Members vs Shareholders, SFIO, DIN via SPICe+
questions.note: Students must attempt ALL parts of either Q.4 OR Q.4A

sub_questions.question_text: Moon Ltd. terminated Mr. Ranjan (investigation pending) after 30 days of application to Tribunal without reply. Is termination valid?

key_points: Section 218 CA 2013: Company requires approval of Tribunal before termination/suspension/punishment/adverse change in terms of employment of employee when investigation is pending
Tribunal must notify objection in WRITING
If company does NOT receive approval within 30 DAYS of application: it MAY PROCEED to take the action
In this case, 30 days passed without reply → Company CAN proceed
Termination is VALID
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: Under S.218 CA 2013, if the Tribunal does not respond within 30 days of the application, the company may proceed with the action. Moon Ltd.'s termination of Mr. Ranjan after 30 days without Tribunal reply is VALID.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: S.218 + 30-day deemed approval + valid conclusion
evaluation_criteria.good: Correct conclusion with 30-day rule
evaluation_criteria.partial: Correct conclusion without specific provision

sub_questions.question_text: What remedy is available to Mr. Ranjan (where Tribunal has NOT replied)?

key_points: Appeal to Appellate Tribunal under S.218 CA 2013 can be made only if the person is DISSATISFIED WITH THE OBJECTION RAISED BY TRIBUNAL
In this case, Tribunal did NOT reply → No objection raised
Mr. Ranjan CANNOT prefer an appeal to Appellate Tribunal
No remedy available to Mr. Ranjan in this scenario
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: Since the Tribunal did not reply (and thus raised no objection), Mr. Ranjan cannot appeal to the Appellate Tribunal (appeal only lies against Tribunal's objection). Mr. Ranjan has NO remedy available.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: Correctly states no remedy as Tribunal did not raise objection (appeal only against Tribunal's objection)
evaluation_criteria.good: Correct conclusion with reasoning
evaluation_criteria.partial: Says no remedy but incomplete reasoning

sub_questions.question_text: What remedy for Mr. Ranjan if Tribunal replied within 30 days?

key_points: If Tribunal replied with objection within 30 days
Company or person concerned if DISSATISFIED with the objection can prefer APPEAL to APPELLATE TRIBUNAL within 30 DAYS of receipt of notice of objection
Mr. Ranjan can prefer an appeal to the Appellate Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the Tribunal's objection letter
Decision of Appellate Tribunal is FINAL AND BINDING on the Tribunal and company
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: If the Tribunal raised an objection within 30 days, Mr. Ranjan can prefer an appeal to the Appellate Tribunal within 30 days of receiving the notice of objection. The Appellate Tribunal's decision shall be final and binding.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: Appeal to Appellate Tribunal + within 30 days of objection + binding nature of decision
evaluation_criteria.good: Appeal to Appellate Tribunal within 30 days
evaluation_criteria.partial: Appeal available but wrong tribunal or timeline

sub_questions.question_text: Ankur Steel Ltd. raised ₹400 crore from public issue for steel unit in Odisha; utilized ₹100 crore. Now wants to use remaining ₹300 crore for software development (AI) by adding new object in MOA. Can it do so? If yes, what steps?

key_points: Section 13(8) CA 2013: A company that has raised money from public through prospectus and has ANY UNUTILIZED AMOUNT shall NOT change its objects UNLESS a SPECIAL RESOLUTION is passed AND:
(i) Details of special resolution published in newspapers (one English, one vernacular) in circulation at place of registered office AND on company's website, with JUSTIFICATION for change
(ii) DISSENTING SHAREHOLDERS must be given opportunity to EXIT by promoters and shareholders having control, in accordance with SEBI regulations
Section 13(9): Registrar shall register alteration of MOA re: objects and certify within 30 DAYS from filing of special resolution
Section 13(10): No alteration shall have effect until registered
Conclusion: YES, the company CAN add the object for software development and use the unutilized funds, but must comply with the above requirements
legal_provisions: SEBI regulations on exit opportunity for dissenting shareholders
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: Under S.13(8) CA 2013, the company CAN change its objects but must: pass a special resolution, publish details in newspapers (English + vernacular) with justification, place on website, and give dissenting shareholders an exit opportunity per SEBI regulations. Post special resolution filing, Registrar certifies within 30 days. Change has no effect until registered.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: S.13(8) + special resolution + newspaper publication + dissenting shareholders' exit opportunity + 30-day registration + no effect until registered
evaluation_criteria.good: S.13(8) + special resolution + dissenting shareholders + Registrar registration
evaluation_criteria.partial: Special resolution mentioned but incomplete steps

sub_questions.question_text: Analyse eligibility of a minor to become member in 4 scenarios: (i) Agreement signed by minor; (ii) Allotment/transfer of fully paid-up shares through guardian; (iii) Transfer of partly paid-up shares and future call liability; (iv) Dividend restoration on repudiation upon majority.

key_points: (i) Minor by agreement: Minor wholly incompetent to contract. Agreement by minor to take shares is VOID AB INITIO. Minor CANNOT become member by agreement signed by him

(ii) Minor through guardian – fully paid-up shares: Written agreement signed by lawful guardian on minor's behalf is valid. Registration of transfer of FULLY PAID-UP shares in name of minor acting through guardian CANNOT be refused on ground of minority. [Miss Nandita Jain v. Benett Coleman, 1978]. Minor CAN become member through guardian for fully paid-up shares
(iii) Partly paid-up shares transferred to minor: Transferor REMAINS LIABLE for all future calls on such shares as long as held by minor, EVEN IF transferor was ignorant of minority

(iv) Dividend restoration on repudiation: Minor is NOT required to restore dividend received during minority upon repudiation of membership on attaining majority. Company CANNOT invoke doctrine of estoppel against him. [Sadiq Ali v. Jai Kishori (1928)]
legal_provisions: Miss Nandita Jain v. Benett Coleman and Co. Ltd. (1978)
Sadiq Ali v. Jai Kishori (1928) 30 Bom. L.R. 1346
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: (i) Void ab initio – minor cannot. (ii) Valid through guardian for fully paid shares (Nandita Jain case). (iii) Transferor liable for future calls on partly paid shares even if ignorant of minority. (iv) No restoration of dividend on repudiation; no estoppel against minor (Sadiq Ali case).

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: All 4 scenarios correctly answered with case citations where applicable
evaluation_criteria.good: 3 out of 4 scenarios correctly answered
evaluation_criteria.partial: 2 out of 4 scenarios correctly answered

questions.topic: Case Study – ABC Limited AGM (Notice, Quorum, Proxy, Special Resolution)
questions.case_context: ABC Limited (not listed) with 800 members and quorum fixed at 7 members in AOA. 1st AGM called on 24th December 2021 at 2:30 PM. Notice issued on 1st December 2021. AGM was for adoption of FS, appointment of directors etc. Record date/Cut-off: 17th December 2021.

sub_questions.question_text: Notice issued 1st December 2021 for AGM on 24th December 2021. Sent by post. Check validity.

key_points: Section 101(1) CA 2013: General meeting requires not less than 21 CLEAR DAYS' notice
SS-2 Para 1.2.6: For 21 clear days, EXCLUDE (1) day of sending notice AND (2) day of meeting AND (3) 2 additional days for SERVICE if sent by post or courier
Day of dispatch: 1st December 2021 (excluded)
Day of AGM: 24th December 2021 (excluded)
Days for service of notice by post: 2nd and 3rd December 2021 (excluded)
Effective notice period: 4th December 2021 to 23rd December 2021 = 20 days
Required: 21 clear days
Short by: 1 day
Conclusion: Notice is NOT VALID – falls short by 1 day
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: Excluding day of dispatch (1 Dec), day of AGM (24 Dec), and 2 service days for post (2 & 3 Dec), only 20 clear days remain (4 Dec to 23 Dec). The required 21 clear days are not met. Notice is NOT VALID, short by 1 day.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: Correct exclusion of all 4 days (dispatch + AGM + 2 service days) + count of 20 days + short by 1 day + invalid conclusion
evaluation_criteria.good: Correct count and conclusion with SS-2 reference
evaluation_criteria.partial: Correct conclusion but missed one exclusion

sub_questions.question_text: Check whether quorum of AGM is validly constituted based on: Mr. A (representative of Governor of Gujarat), Mr. B & C (preference shareholders), Mr. D (representing PQR Ltd. and XYZ Ltd.), Mr. E, F, G, H (proxies of shareholders).

key_points: Mr. A (representative of Governor): Treated as member personally present (Section 112 CA 2013). Counts as 1 member

Mr. B & C (preference shareholders): Can vote ONLY on matters directly affecting their rights (S.47). Adoption of FS and appointment of directors does NOT affect their rights. B & C CANNOT be counted for quorum purposes

Mr. D (representing PQR Ltd. and XYZ Ltd.): Corporate representative counts as one member for each body corporate represented. Mr. D represents 2 body corporates (S.113). Counts as 2 members personally present
Mr. E, F, G, H (proxies): Proxies do NOT count for quorum (S.105). Only PERSONAL PRESENCE counts
Total members personally present for quorum: 1 (A) + 0 (B,C) + 2 (D for two companies) = 3 members
AOA quorum: 7 members
Legal quorum under S.103(1)(a)(i) for public company with ≤ 1000 members: 5 members personally present
Conclusion: Only 3 members personally present → Does NOT constitute proper quorum (neither AOA quorum of 7 nor statutory quorum of 5 is met)
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: Only 3 members qualify for quorum: Mr. A (S.112, counts as 1), Mr. D representing 2 companies (S.113, counts as 2). B & C (preference shareholders – restricted voting) and E, F, G, H (proxies, S.105) don't count. With 800 members, statutory quorum is 5; AOA quorum is 7. Only 3 present → QUORUM NOT MET.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: Correctly analyses all 4 categories + arrives at 3 members + both statutory and AOA quorum not met
evaluation_criteria.good: Correctly analyses 3 categories + quorum not met conclusion
evaluation_criteria.partial: Correctly analyses 2 categories + correct conclusion
evaluation_criteria.minimal: Just says quorum not met without analysis

sub_questions.question_text: Mr. S issued two proxies – X (lodged 22 Dec at 10 AM) and Y (lodged 23 Dec at 3:30 PM). Company rejected both. Is rejection in order? Also state provisions on inspection of proxies.

key_points: Section 105 CA 2013 + SS-2 Para 6.6.1: Proxy must be deposited 48 HOURS before the time of the meeting
AGM: 24 Dec 2021 at 2:30 PM → deadline for proxy: 22 Dec 2021 at 2:30 PM
Proxy for Mr. X: Deposited 22 Dec at 10 AM → BEFORE 2:30 PM on 22 Dec → VALID
Proxy for Mr. Y: Deposited 23 Dec at 3:30 PM → AFTER the 48-hour deadline → INVALID
SS-2: Where multiple proxies received for same holdings, proxy DATED LAST is considered valid
In this case, proxy for Y is invalid (late) → proxy for X is valid
Rejecting proxy for X is UNSUSTAINABLE (X's proxy is valid)
Rejecting proxy for Y is CORRECT (Y's proxy is invalid being less than 48 hours before meeting)
INSPECTION OF PROXIES:
Section 105(8): Every member entitled to vote may inspect proxies lodged, if at least 3 DAYS' notice in writing given to company (received at least 3 days before meeting)
SS-2 Para 6.8.2: Proxies available for inspection during period BEGINNING 24 HOURS before meeting commencement and ENDING at conclusion of meeting
Inspection allowed between 9 AM and 6 PM during that period
Any member entitled to vote on any resolution may inspect
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: 48-hour deadline: 22 Dec at 2:30 PM. X's proxy (10 AM on 22 Dec) = VALID. Y's proxy (23 Dec at 3:30 PM) = INVALID. Rejecting X's proxy is WRONG; rejecting Y's proxy is CORRECT. Inspection: 3 days' written notice to company; available 24 hours before meeting to conclusion of meeting, between 9 AM and 6 PM.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: 48-hour deadline calculation + X valid + Y invalid + X rejection unsustainable + Y rejection correct + full inspection provisions
evaluation_criteria.good: Correct analysis of both proxies + partial inspection provisions
evaluation_criteria.partial: Correct conclusion on proxies but incomplete inspection provisions
evaluation_criteria.minimal: Only says one proxy valid/invalid without calculation

sub_questions.question_text: 400 members present. 200 voted in favour, 50 against, 50 invalid, 100 abstained for special resolution. Chairman declared resolution passed. Validity?

key_points: Section 114(2) CA 2013: Special resolution requires votes in FAVOUR to be NOT LESS THAN THREE TIMES the votes AGAINST
Invalid votes and abstentions are NOT COUNTED
Valid votes cast: 200 (favour) + 50 (against) = 250
Invalid votes (50) and abstentions (100) are excluded
Votes in favour: 200
Votes against: 50
Ratio: 200/50 = 4:1 (which is more than 3:1 required)
OR: 200/250 = 80% (more than 75% = 3/4 required)
Conclusion: Special resolution is VALIDLY PASSED. Chairman's declaration is VALID
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: Under S.114(2), special resolution requires at least 3x votes in favour vs against. Valid votes: 200 favour, 50 against (invalid and abstentions excluded). Ratio 200:50 = 4:1 > required 3:1. OR 80% > 75%. Special resolution VALIDLY PASSED. Chairman's declaration is VALID.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: S.114(2) + excludes invalid and abstentions + correct calculation (200 vs 50) + 3:1 or 75% test + valid conclusion
evaluation_criteria.good: S.114(2) + correct calculation + valid conclusion
evaluation_criteria.partial: Correct conclusion but includes invalid votes in calculation

questions.topic: Drafting – Board Resolutions, Circular Resolution, EGM Notice, CSR Policy – OR – Short Notice Board Meeting, Small Shareholders Director, Borrowing Powers, Charitable Contribution
questions.note: Drafting questions – marks awarded for correct format, legal accuracy, completeness, and relevant provisions cited. Students must attempt ALL parts of Q.6 OR Q.6A.

sub_questions.question_text: Draft board resolution constituting Audit Committee – members, chairman, quorum, 2 functions.

key_points: Cites Section 177 CA 2013
Committee must have minimum 3 directors with majority being INDEPENDENT DIRECTORS
All members should be financially literate; chairperson should have accounting/financial management expertise
Chairman must be independent director
Chairman of Audit Committee to be present at AGM to answer shareholder queries
Quorum: At least 3 directors of whom at least 2 shall be INDEPENDENT DIRECTORS

Functions: (1) Recommendation for appointment/remuneration/terms of appointment of auditors; (2) Review and monitor independence and performance of auditors; (3) Review quarterly/annual financial statements and submit to Board with recommendation
Format: 'RESOLVED THAT...' 'RESOLVED FURTHER THAT...' structure
Mention chairperson of audit committee to attend AGM
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: Resolution to cite S.177 CA 2013. Constitution with minimum 3 members (majority IDs). ID as chairperson. Quorum = 3 members with at least 2 IDs. Two functions from S.177(4). Proper 'RESOLVED THAT' and 'RESOLVED FURTHER THAT' format.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: S.177 cited + correct composition + ID chairperson + correct quorum + 2 valid functions + proper resolution format
evaluation_criteria.good: S.177 + mostly correct composition + 2 functions in proper format
evaluation_criteria.partial: Correct format but missing quorum or composition accuracy
evaluation_criteria.minimal: Vague resolution without proper legal structure

sub_questions.question_text: Draft resolution by circulation for appointment of Vikram as Additional Director under Section 161 CA 2013.

key_points: Section 175 CA 2013 governs resolution by circulation
Section 161 CA 2013 governs additional director appointment
Format: Covering letter with resolution + brief note
Resolution must mention: appointment effective date, tenure up to next AGM or last date on which AGM should have been held
Must seek *Assent/Dissent/Require Meeting from each director
Brief note must include: urgency/necessity for circulation, Vikram's qualifications (M.Tech, MBA IIM), experience, DIN, consent
Directors to respond within 7 days
Must mention: none of directors interested in resolution
Signed by MD/CS
All directors requested to return within 7 days
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: Resolution by circulation format: Letter to each director, draft resolution citing S.161, Vikram's DIN and appointment date, tenure till next AGM. Assent/Dissent/Require Meeting option. Brief note explaining urgency. Return within 7 days. Signed by MD or CS.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: S.175 + S.161 cited + proper format with all elements (letter + resolution + brief note + Assent/Dissent option + 7-day deadline)
evaluation_criteria.good: Proper format with most elements and S.161 cited
evaluation_criteria.partial: Correct format but missing some elements or S.175
evaluation_criteria.minimal: Just a plain resolution without circulation format

sub_questions.question_text: Draft notice of EGM for removal of director Srinivasan on requisition of member Revati holding 5% shares, to be issued on 1st December 2023.

key_points: EGM on 30 December 2023 at 10 AM at registered office, Hyderabad
Notice to be issued on requisition of Ms. Revati (50,000 equity shares = 5% voting capital)
Special notice received under Section 115 CA 2013 for removal of director
Resolution to be passed under Section 115 read with Section 169 CA 2013
Ordinary Resolution for removal (Section 169 requires only ordinary resolution)
Must include: Details of meeting, special notice, resolution, authorisation clause
Notes: Proxy provisions, corporate representative, proxy deposit 48 hours before, explanatory statement under S.102
Explanatory Statement: Details of special notice, basis for removal (fraudulent activities), conflict of interest statement, Board recommendation
Signed by Company Secretary, dated 1st December 2023
Resolution to include authority to file DIR-12 with ROC
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: Notice format: EGM on 30 Dec 2023, 10 AM at Hyderabad registered office. Requisition by Revati (5%). Ordinary Resolution under S.115 read with S.169 for removal of Srinivasan. Standard notes on proxy, 48-hour deposit. Explanatory statement under S.102 with details of special notice, grounds for removal, Board recommendation.

evaluation_criteria.full_marks: Correct format + S.115 and S.169 cited + EGM details + ordinary resolution + notes + full explanatory statement under S.102
evaluation_criteria.good: Correct format + most elements + S.115 and S.169
evaluation_criteria.partial: Correct format but incomplete legal provisions or missing explanatory statement
evaluation_criteria.minimal: Basic notice without proper legal basis or notes

sub_questions.question_text: Draft board resolution to approve and adopt a new CSR Policy of Himachal Chemicals Limited.

key_points: Cites Section 135 CA 2013 + Companies (CSR Policy) Rules 2014 + Amendment Rules 2021
Based on recommendation of CSR Committee
Approves new CSR Policy in suppression of existing policy dated ...
Signed by Director for identification
Authority granted to Directors/CS/CFO to take necessary steps
Includes disseminating revised policy on company's website
Proper 'RESOLVED THAT' and 'RESOLVED FURTHER THAT' format
expected_answer.full_answer_summary: Board resolution approving new CSR Policy citing S.135 and CSR Rules (including 2021 amendments), based on CSR Committee recommendation, in suppression of earlier policy, with authority to CS/CFO/Directors to implement and disseminate on website.
